rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results (Tables 3-9) - the authors report their own field experiments on five furrow irrigation methods (conventional, surge, alternate) in maize in the Jayder Plain, Iran, during the 2021 season, with WinSRFR calibration, sensitivity analysis and performance indicators.
rows.notes: The study contains no drip or drip fertigation treatment and nothing about subsurface laterals, evaporation or nutrients. It evaluates surface furrow irrigation methods (CFI, SFI, FFI, AFI) and reports that variable alternate furrow irrigation had the highest application efficiency (78.7%) and lowest runoff (19.5%) versus conventional furrow (62.0%, 35.7%), and that WinSRFR iso-performance optimisation of inflow rate and cutoff time could raise application efficiency by about 8 percentage points. It therefore provides no evidence of its own on drip fertigation minimising runoff or reducing evaporation; the cited technology is a different one.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract and reference list absent but all main sections present). The study concerns surge and alternate furrow irrigation evaluated with WinSRFR, not drip fertigation.
